questions.question: Describe the origin, composition and main producers of cotton fibre.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the origin, composition and main producers of cotton fibre.
  • Cotton is a natural seed type vegetable fibre called the “King of Fibres.” It is composed mainly of
  • cellulose (90–94%). Cotton fibres are obtained from the seeds of the cotton plant. Main producers of
  • cotton are USA, Russia, Brazil, Egypt, India, Pakistan and China. Egypt produces the best quality
  • cotton.
questions.final_answer: cotton.

questions.question: Describe the physical properties of wool fibre such as colour, strength, elasticity and crimp.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the physical properties of wool fibre such as colour, strength, elasticity and crimp.
  • • Colour: Cream, yellow and grey-yellow.
  • • Strength: Wool has poor strength with tenacity of 1–2 gpd. Strength decreases by 25% on
  • wetting.
  • • Elasticity: Wool has excellent elasticity due to its wavy structure and scales. It can stretch up
  • to 30% before breaking.
  • • Crimp: Wool has natural crimp or waves which increase cohesiveness, resiliency and
  • insulation.
questions.final_answer: insulation.

questions.question: Explain seed, leaf and bast fibres with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain seed, leaf and bast fibres with examples.
  • • Seed fibres: Fibres collected from seeds or seed cases. Example: cotton and kapok.
  • • Leaf fibres: Fibres collected from leaves. Example: sisal and agaves.
  • • Bast fibres: Fibres collected from the skin or bast surrounding the stem of plants. They have
  • high tensile strength. Examples: flax, jute, hemp and ramie.
questions.final_answer: high tensile strength. Examples: flax, jute, hemp and ramie.

questions.question: Explain why technical specifications are used instead of common names in the woven fabric industry.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why technical specifications are used instead of common names in the woven fabric
  • industry.
  • Common names of fabrics may vary in meaning from one country to another, causing confusion in
  • trade. Therefore, technical specifications are used for accurate identification and communication.
  • Technical specifications include:
  • • Fabric width
  • • Ends per inch and picks per inch
  • • Weave type
  • • Fibre content
  • • Warp and weft count
  • • GSM
  • • Type of finish applied
  • These provide clear and uniform information about the fabric.
questions.final_answer: These provide clear and uniform information about the fabric.

questions.question: Discuss screen printing in detail including process, types, characteristics, advantages and disadvantages.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss screen printing in detail including process, types, characteristics, advantages and
  • disadvantages.
  • Screen printing is the most widely used method of textile printing. Screens made of silk or nylon
  • mesh stretched over wooden frames are used.
  • Process
  • • Screen is prepared by blocking non-design areas.
  • • Screen is placed over fabric.
  • • Printing paste is spread using a squeegee.
  • • Dye passes through open design areas onto fabric.
  • Types
  • • Manual flat screen printing
  • • Mechanical flat screen printing
  • • Rotary screen printing
  • Characteristics
  • • Suitable for multicolour designs
  • • Faster than block printing
  • • Good print quality
  • Advantages
  • • Can print large designs
  • • Suitable for many fabrics
  • • Better colour application
  • Disadvantages
  • • Slower than roller printing
  • • Separate screen needed for each colour
questions.final_answer: • Separate screen needed for each colour

questions.question: Explain absorbency, lustre, flexibility and abrasion resistance of textile fibres with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain absorbency, lustre, flexibility and abrasion resistance of textile fibres with suitable
  • examples.
  • Absorbency
  • Absorbency is the ability of a fibre to take up moisture. It is expressed as moisture regain percentage.
  • Fibres with good absorbency are comfortable and dye well. Cotton has excellent absorbency due to
  • high cellulose content and air-filled lumen. Wool can absorb up to 20% moisture without feeling
  • damp.
  • Lustre
  • Lustre is the shine or brightness of a fibre caused by reflection of light. Smooth and round fibres
  • reflect more light. Silk has excellent lustre because of its smooth surface and triangular cross-section.
  • Cotton has little or no lustre.
  • Flexibility
  • Flexibility or pliability is the ease with which fibres bend or twist. Flexible fibres can be easily spun
  • into yarns and resist breaking during folding. Wool and silk are flexible fibres, while flax is
  • comparatively stiff.
  • Abrasion Resistance
  • Abrasion resistance is the ability of a fibre to withstand rubbing during use. Toughness, smoothness
  • and pliability improve abrasion resistance. Flax has good abrasion resistance. Fibres with high
  • abrasion resistance produce durable fabrics.
questions.final_answer: abrasion resistance produce durable fabrics.

questions.question: Explain the importance of synchronization of shedding, picking, and beat-up in fabric production.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of synchronization of shedding, picking, and beat-up in fabric
  • production.
  • Fabric production on a loom depends on proper synchronization of the three basic loom motions:
  • Shedding
  • Warp yarns are separated to form a shed through which weft yarn passes.
  • Picking
  • Weft yarn is inserted through the open shed.
  • Beat-up
  • The reed pushes the newly inserted weft into the fabric structure.
  • Importance of Synchronization
  • • Ensures smooth weaving process
  • • Prevents yarn breakage and fabric defects
  • • Maintains correct fabric structure and density
  • • Improves production efficiency and fabric quality
  • • Proper timing ensures accurate interlacement of warp and weft yarns.
questions.final_answer: • Proper timing ensures accurate interlacement of warp and weft yarns.

questions.question: Explain block printing and discharge printing in detail.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain block printing and discharge printing in detail.
  • Block Printing
  • Block printing is a direct style and hand printing process using engraved wooden blocks.
  • Process
  • • Design is carved on wooden blocks.
  • • Fabric is prepared and dye spread on tray.
  • • Block is dipped into dye and pressed onto fabric repeatedly.
  • • Fabric is dried and fixed.
  • Advantages
  • • Decorative and artistic prints
  • • Eco-friendly when natural dyes are used
  • • Unique handcrafted appearance
  • Disadvantages
  • • Slow and labour-intensive
  • • Expensive due to hand process
  • • Difficult to obtain shading effects
  • • Gaps may remain between prints
  • Discharge Printing
questions.final_answer: Discharge Printing
